content:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Lifecycle sprint mid-point metrics review (activation + guardrails)
Date: 2026-01-23
Time: 9:00 AM PT
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees:
- Ben Carter (Growth Marketing)
- Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops & Attribution)
- Marissa Cole (Product - Console)

Auto-Summary (generated)
- Reviewed early activation lift from onboarding emails and console nudges.
- Flagged two data quality issues impacting attribution + event counts (UTM property missing on a slice; streaming success event delayed).
- Guardrail check: small unsubscribe uptick and one suppression edge case under investigation.
- Support volume stable; one recurring issue around API key permissions / project roles.
- Agreed to iterate on Email #2 subject lines and adjust console copy for permissions confusion.

Topics
1) Activation funnel: 24h/72h activation and time-to-first-success
2) Console nudges: checklist engagement, banner CTR, error-help clicks
3) Retargeting: early CTR/CVR (directional only)
4) Guardrails: unsubscribes, complaints, support tickets, console perf
5) Instrumentation gaps and dashboard definitions

Action Items (generated)
- Tyler to validate unsubscribe suppression and deliverability metrics; confirm resolution.
- Marissa to propose copy tweak + trigger change for permissions confusion.
- Ben to update email subject line variants and throttle until guardrails are green.

Questions (open)
- Do we define activation as first 2xx completion (non-streaming) or first streaming success for the sprint decision?
- Should “dashboard_viewed” be a tertiary milestone or a guardrail signal only?

Transcript

[00:00] Ben Carter: Alright, cool. Thanks for jumping. This is the mid-sprint metrics review. Goal is, uh, check early activation movement, make sure guardrails aren’t screaming, and then decide what we tweak for week two.

[00:12] Tyler Benson: Yep. I’ve got the Looker board up. Also the email dashboard, like, provider-level deliverability.

[00:18] Marissa Cole: And I can pull up the console events view. I’m mostly watching checklist impressions, completion rate, and any perf regressions from the component.

[00:28] Ben Carter: Great. Let’s start with the primary thing. Tyler, can you walk us through activation within 24 and 72?

[00:35] Tyler Benson: Yep. So, cohort is self-serve new signups starting Monday 00:00 UTC. Randomization is at user_id. For the email sequence v1, we’re seeing activation within 24 hours at 18.9% in control vs 22.1% in treatment.

[00:51] Ben Carter: Nice.

[00:52] Tyler Benson: It’s early, so, confidence is… it’s like trending, not a slam dunk. But the direction is consistent when I cut by SDK: TypeScript looks better than Python, weirdly.

[01:03] Marissa Cole: Could be the TS SDK PR we shipped. The “hello inference” example improved the errors.

[01:08] Tyler Benson: Yeah, that’s a good point. Time-to-first-success median went from 47 minutes to 39 minutes in treatment. That’s across email + nudges combined for the “full” audience.

[01:20] Ben Carter: And when you isolate just email?

[01:22] Tyler Benson: That’s where it gets messy. There’s some contamination because console nudges are assigned separately and a chunk of users hit both.

[01:30] Ben Carter: Right, right. But directionally, good.

[01:33] Tyler Benson: For 72 hours activation, control is 27.4% and treatment is 31.0%. Again, small n.

[01:43] Ben Carter: Okay. Marissa, what are we seeing with nudges? Checklist and banners.

[01:49] Marissa Cole: So for the checklist component: impression rate is high, like 86% of eligible new users see it at least once. The completion rate of the checklist… depends how you count. If completion means “API key created + first request success” it’s 34% treatment vs 31% control.

[02:09] Ben Carter: Wait, why control has checklist? Sorry.

[02:12] Marissa Cole: Sorry, sorry. Control here is “no checklist” but they can still activate obviously. I’m comparing activation among eligible users, not checklist completion. The thing that’s more telling is checklist interaction: 41% clicked at least one step.

[02:28] Tyler Benson: And step click-through correlates with activation pretty strongly.

[02:32] Marissa Cole: Yeah. The top clicked step is “Create API key,” then “Run first request.” Streaming step is lower. A bunch of folks don’t bother enabling streaming initially.

[02:43] Ben Carter: Which is fine. We said primary activation is first success request. Secondary is first streaming success.

[02:48] Tyler Benson: Yeah, but about that, I need to flag: “first_streaming_success” event is undercounting. I think we’re missing it for Python because of an SDK version not emitting the right property.

[02:59] Marissa Cole: That lines up with what Eng saw. There was a hotfix thread about a missing property or wrong trigger.

[03:05] Tyler Benson: Exactly. So any read on streaming should be treated as “directional only” until we confirm event parity.

[03:13] Ben Carter: Got it. Let’s table streaming metric for decision-making right now.

[03:17] Ben Carter: Guardrails next. Unsubscribes, tickets, and console health. Tyler, email first.

[03:23] Tyler Benson: Unsubscribe rate: control is basically baseline. Treatment is up about 0.12 percentage points. Not huge, but it’s a change.

[03:33] Ben Carter: Is that within our guardrail threshold?

[03:35] Tyler Benson: Technically yes. We said +0.2pp is where we pause. But the more concerning thing is we got one complaint that looks like someone opted out and still received Email #3.

[03:46] Ben Carter: That’s the suppression bug, right?

[03:48] Tyler Benson: Yeah. Support logged something similar. I’m tracing it. It might be an edge case with “marketing opt-out” syncing late. Or we’re not reading the suppression list in time if someone signs up and opts out same day.

[04:04] Marissa Cole: Compliance-wise, we need to be careful. If it’s real, we should pause sending to that slice until fixed.

[04:10] Ben Carter: Agree. Tyler, can you confirm by end of day? And I’ll reduce throttle for the non-activated segment until we’re sure.

[04:18] Tyler Benson: Yep. I’ll pull raw sends + opt-out timestamps.

[04:22] Ben Carter: Deliverability otherwise okay?

[04:24] Tyler Benson: Mostly. SPF/DKIM alignment is okay, but Gmail tab placement got slightly worse this week. Not catastrophic. Complaint rate is still low.

[04:35] Ben Carter: Okay.

[04:36] Ben Carter: Marissa, console performance guardrail?

[04:39] Marissa Cole: No issues so far. Load time and error rates stable. The checklist component is behind a flag and it’s simple. We’re tracking “banner_render_ms” to be safe and it’s not trending up.

[04:52] Ben Carter: Support volume? I saw a ping about 404 links.

[04:56] Marissa Cole: That’s not directly console, but yeah. Email links to the console route changed and some deep links hit a 404. That’s a docs/route mismatch.

[05:06] Tyler Benson: I saw that ticket too. If folks click from Email #1 CTA to “Create key” and it 404’s, that’s brutal.

[05:13] Ben Carter: Is it fixed?

[05:15] Marissa Cole: There’s a patch to redirect, but I don’t know if it’s fully deployed. I’ll check with Chloe.

[05:23] Ben Carter: Please. That’s an activation killer.

[05:26] Tyler Benson: Also, the UTM capture for that link: some clicks arrive without UTMs because the docs site strips query params in one redirect.

[05:35] Ben Carter: Ugh. Okay, so that’s why attribution looks weird.

[05:39] Tyler Benson: Exactly. I can’t reliably join touch to activation event for that path.

[05:44] Ben Carter: So immediate fixes: route redirect and preserve UTMs.

[05:48] Marissa Cole: Yep.

[05:50] Ben Carter: Let’s talk about what we change week two. I’m thinking subject lines, and maybe cut one email if unsub is trending.

[05:58] Tyler Benson: I wouldn’t cut yet. The unsubscribe uptick might be from that suppression edge case. But I do think Email #2 subject line is underperforming. Open rate is 31% vs 38% for Email #1.

[06:10] Ben Carter: Which is the “Your first production-like call” one.

[06:13] Tyler Benson: Yeah. The subject line is currently “Get your first successful call in 5 minutes” and some folks might read it as scammy.

[06:21] Ben Carter: Okay, what are the variants we approved?

[06:24] Tyler Benson: Variant B: “Make your first request (copy/paste curl)” and Variant C: “Quickstart: API key → first response”. More literal.

[06:33] Marissa Cole: I like the literal one. Developer tone.

[06:36] Ben Carter: Cool, we’ll roll that.

[06:38] Ben Carter: On console nudges: any copy issues?

[06:41] Marissa Cole: Yes. We have a recurring issue: users create an API key but then get a permissions error because they’re in the wrong project or their role doesn’t allow key creation. The banner today says “Create an API key” which is wrong when they already did.

[06:59] Tyler Benson: That shows up in events as “api_key_created” then “request_error_401” repeated.

[07:05] Marissa Cole: Exactly. We should show a just-in-time help state: “Key created, but you may not have access to this project route. Check project selection / org role.”

[07:17] Ben Carter: Do we have a support doc we can link?

[07:19] Marissa Cole: We can link to troubleshooting. Or a short inline tooltip with steps.

[07:25] Tyler Benson: From measurement, we can tag “support_link_click” and see if it spikes.

[07:30] Ben Carter: Let’s do minimal copy change now. Don’t ship a huge UI.

[07:34] Marissa Cole: Agreed. I’ll draft copy and we’ll keep it behind the flag.

[07:40] Ben Carter: Retargeting quick pulse — Tyler?

[07:43] Tyler Benson: Early days. LinkedIn CTR is okay, like 0.7%. Google is lower. CVR to signup is okay-ish, but again, attribution is shaky because of UTMs stripping on one landing page variant.

[07:57] Ben Carter: So focus on fixing tracking before optimizing creative.

[08:00] Tyler Benson: Yeah. Otherwise we’re flying blind.

[08:05] Ben Carter: Anything else guardrail wise? Complaints? Support spike?

[08:10] Marissa Cole: Support volume is stable, but the top topic is “why do I need billing to do X?” It’s probably from the “add billing for higher limits” nudge. Some folks interpret it as required to just try the API.

[08:24] Ben Carter: That’s not good. We should ensure we don’t gate basic activation behind billing messaging.

[08:29] Tyler Benson: We can change the copy to “Optional: add billing to remove free-tier limits” and keep it as a later step.

[08:36] Marissa Cole: I can also change trigger rules so billing banner only shows after first success. Right now it can show too early.

[08:44] Ben Carter: Yes. Let’s do that.

[08:47] Tyler Benson: Measurement wise, we can track “billing_banner_impression” and ensure it’s not showing pre-activation.

[08:53] Ben Carter: Great.

[09:00] Ben Carter: Now, I want to sanity check: are we aligned that primary activation metric for the sprint decision is first_request_success (2xx completion), not streaming? Given the instrumentation issue.

[09:12] Tyler Benson: Yes. And we can keep first_streaming_success as secondary once fixed.

[09:16] Marissa Cole: Agree.

[09:18] Ben Carter: Okay.

[09:20] Tyler Benson: One more thing: dashboard_viewed. It’s up in treatment because Email #4 pushes “see your cost breakdown”. But does it matter?

[09:28] Ben Carter: It’s a milestone for retention maybe.

[09:31] Marissa Cole: I think it matters as an engagement proxy. But not the activation definition.

[09:36] Tyler Benson: Right. And it’s not a guardrail unless it correlates with something bad.

[09:40] Ben Carter: Cool.

[09:42] Ben Carter: Let’s do a quick recap of numbers we’ll share in #general or in the readout outline.

[09:48] Tyler Benson: Activation within 24h: +3.2pp-ish in treatment. Time-to-first-success median down ~8 minutes. D7 retention is not readable yet; too early.

[09:58] Ben Carter: Any negative signals?

[10:00] Tyler Benson: Slight unsubscribe uptick and the one suppression edge case. Also link 404s and UTMs stripped, which is like operational not user preference.

[10:09] Marissa Cole: And permissions confusion causing 401 loops. That’s user friction.

[10:14] Ben Carter: Great. Week two plan is: fix the 404/redirect and UTM preservation, adjust billing nudge trigger to post-activation, update banner copy for permissions confusion, swap Email #2 subject line.

[10:28] Tyler Benson: Plus I’ll validate streaming event coverage and that utm_campaign property is present on first_request_success.

[10:34] Ben Carter: Yep.

[10:35] Marissa Cole: I’ll ping Chloe and Jada about timeline. This is all feature-flagged so should be safe.

[10:43] Ben Carter: Perfect.

[10:45] Tyler Benson: Should we pause any audience expansion until suppression is confirmed fixed?

[10:49] Ben Carter: Not a full pause, but I’ll reduce throttle for the non-activated. And if you confirm it’s a real opt-out violation, we stop that sequence until fixed.

[11:00] Tyler Benson: Got it.

[11:02] Ben Carter: Alright. Anything else before we drop?

[11:05] Marissa Cole: Just one note: some user sessions are attributed to “unknown SDK”. That might be because curl requests don’t set the header.

[11:12] Tyler Benson: Yeah, that’s expected. But we can improve docs to recommend setting the header in examples.

[11:17] Ben Carter: Not sprint-critical but good backlog.

[11:20] Ben Carter: Okay, thanks both. Tyler post the deliverability + suppression investigation update, Marissa send copy proposal, I’ll update email variants and tracker.

[11:31] Tyler Benson: Sounds good.

[11:32] Marissa Cole: Yep, thanks.

[11:34] Ben Carter: Cool, ending.

[End of transcript]

Notes / Links mentioned (as said on call)
